terms.register: praecipuē apud Plautum; animōs dēspondēre Liv.
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 614: Quaesō hercle, animum nē dēspondē.
Plaut. Mil. 6: nē lāmentētur nēve animum dēspondeat (of a sword)
terms.comment: Animum dēspondēre, to give up one’s courage, to despair, is frequent in Plautus (Lewis & Short); the prohibition with nē and the imperative is the speech of comedy, and in prose nōlī animum dēspondēre.

phrases.latin: Quaesō hercle, animum nē dēspondē. — Nūllust quem dēspondeam.
phrases.english: Please, for heaven’s sake, don’t lose heart. — I’ve no heart left to lose.

phrases.latin: Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.
phrases.english: I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out… That way didn’t work; we’ll go at it another way.

sources: Lewis & Short: despondeo · Lewis & Short: persevero
